questions.q: If Mrs. Chukwu sets up a tailoring shop and keeps her personal savings and shop finances completely separate, which business structure is she most likely using?
options: Private limited liability company
Cooperative society owned by members
Sole proprietorship with separate business account
Partnership with limited partners
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned by one person who can maintain separate business accounts. A private limited company requires registration and shareholders; a partnership involves two or more people; a cooperative is owned by multiple members, so those are incorrect.

questions.q: A company registered in Lagos issues 1,000 ordinary shares at ₦50 each. Later it issues another 500 ordinary shares at ₦80 each. What is the total share capital recorded at nominal (par) value if the nominal value per share is ₦10?
questions.explanation: Nominal (par) value = number of shares × ₦10. Total shares = 1,000 + 500 = 1,500; 1,500 × ₦10 = ₦15,000. The issue prices (₦50, ₦80) affect share premium, not the nominal share capital, so other options are incorrect.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes a private limited liability company from a public limited company in Nigeria?
options: Shares of a private limited company cannot be offered to the general public
Private limited company must publish audited accounts every month
Private limited company cannot make profit
Private limited company requires at least 100,000 employees
questions.explanation: Private limited companies restrict public share offers; public companies may invite the public. Monthly audited accounts and impossible employee counts are false, and private companies can make profit, so those options are wrong.

questions.q: If a buyer in Abuja purchases an electronic stove that stops working within the warranty period, what is the seller legally expected to do under standard consumer protection principles?
options: Charge for repair because the seller sold the product earlier
Tell the buyer warranties are void after first use
Offer only a discount on future purchases
Repair or replace the stove at no extra cost within the warranty terms
questions.explanation: Consumer protection and warranty terms require repair or replacement at no extra cost during warranty. Charging for repair or voiding warranties without valid reason or offering unrelated discounts contradicts warranty obligations.

questions.q: Which government body in Nigeria handles complaints about false trade descriptions and unsafe consumer goods?
options: National Insurance Commission (NAICOM)
Nigerian Stock Exchange (NSE)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON)
questions.explanation: SON enforces product standards and addresses false descriptions and unsafe goods. FRSC is for road safety, NSE deals with capital markets, and NAICOM regulates insurance, so those are incorrect.

questions.q: A Lagos shop advertises ‘Buy one get one free’ but charges for both at the till. Which consumer right is primarily being violated?
options: Right to free education
Right to protection against deceptive advertising
Right to import goods freely
Right to choose a career
questions.explanation: Charging for both items when advertising a free item is deceptive advertising and violates consumer protection. The other listed rights are unrelated to purchase advertising and thus incorrect.

questions.q: A freight firm charges ₦1,200 per ton for the first 3 tons and ₦2,100 per ton for every additional ton. If a customer ships 7 tons, what is the total freight charge?
questions.explanation: First 3 tons: 3 × ₦1,200 = ₦3,600. Additional 4 tons: 4 × ₦2,100 = ₦8,400. Total = ₦3,600 + ₦8,400 = ₦12,000. The tempting ₦14,400 comes from mistakenly using ₦2,400 per ton for all 6 or 7 tons, which is incorrect.

questions.q: Which transport mode is generally most suitable for moving perishable food quickly from Kano to Port Harcourt?
options: Telegraph
Pipeline transport
Inland waterways for the entire route
Air transport
questions.explanation: Air transport is fastest for long-distance perishable goods, reducing spoilage. Pipelines transport liquids/gases, inland waterways cannot cover the full overland route efficiently, and telegraph is communication, not transport.

questions.q: An advertiser in Enugu uses a slogan that implies a toothpaste will 'whiten teeth in one day' without evidence. This is an example of which unethical practice?
options: Market segmentation
Misleading advertising
Corporate social responsibility
Product diversification
questions.explanation: Claiming unproven instant results is misleading advertising. CSR, segmentation, and diversification are legitimate marketing concepts and do not describe deceptive claims.

questions.q: A bakery segments its market by income and offers premium cakes at higher prices to customers in Victoria Island and budget cakes to suburban markets. This is an example of which marketing strategy?
options: Product recall procedure
Random sampling for market research
Selling only through wholesalers
Market segmentation by socioeconomic status
questions.explanation: Charging different prices and targeting areas based on income exemplifies segmentation by socioeconomic status. Random sampling is a research method, recalls are safety procedures, and selling only through wholesalers is a distribution choice, so they are incorrect.

questions.q: A small Lagos boutique uses an online marketplace to sell clothes and collects customer payments via mobile money. Which of the following is the main advantage of selling through an online marketplace compared with having its own website?
options: Guaranteed lower delivery costs for all orders
Access to an existing large customer base and built-in payment systems
Complete control over brand presentation and website layout
Lower commission fees than running a personal website
questions.explanation: Online marketplaces provide sellers immediate access to many buyers and integrated payment and logistics options. Owning a personal website gives more control over presentation, not the marketplace; marketplaces often charge commission fees, and delivery costs are not guaranteed lower.

questions.q: A buyer in Ibadan disputes a smartphone purchase saying it was counterfeit. Under Nigerian e-commerce best practice, which action should the online seller take first?
options: Block the buyer and keep the payment pending indefinitely
Post the buyer's details publicly on social media to warn others
Immediately issue a full refund without enquiring
Request the buyer to provide photos and proof of purchase while investigating the claim
questions.explanation: The correct practice is to investigate with evidence and proof of purchase before refunding. Immediate refunds may be unnecessary; blocking or public shaming are unprofessional and violate dispute-resolution norms.

questions.q: Mr. Adebayo pays an annual life insurance premium of ₦60,000 for a sum assured of ₦3,000,000. Which statement best describes the role of the premium?
options: Premium is a fine charged to the insured for late payment
Premium is the payment by the insured to keep the policy in force and secure the benefit
Premium is the amount the insurer pays to the beneficiary when the insured dies
Premium is the guaranteed investment return the insurer pays annually
questions.explanation: The premium is the insured's periodic payment to maintain coverage. It is not an investment return, the sum assured is the death benefit, and it's not a fine.

questions.q: Which document serves as both a receipt for goods shipped and a document of title allowing the holder to claim goods at destination?
options: Packing list
Bill of lading
Commercial invoice
Pro forma invoice
questions.explanation: A bill of lading acknowledges carriage, acts as a receipt and is a document of title. A pro forma invoice is a preliminary quote, a packing list details contents, and a commercial invoice is for customs and payment but not a title document.

questions.q: A seller in Port Harcourt sends goods to Accra and wants to ensure payment before the buyer receives the shipping documents. Which document/payment term achieves this?
options: Open account
Documents against payment under a documentary collection
Consignment without documents
Cash on delivery (COD) at buyer's warehouse
questions.explanation: Documents against payment (D/P) requires buyer pay before receiving shipping documents. Open account allows shipment without immediate payment; COD at buyer's warehouse is impractical for international sea freight; consignment delays payment until sale.

questions.q: Which occupational sector includes farming, mining and fishing?
options: Primary sector
Secondary sector
Quaternary sector
Tertiary sector
questions.explanation: Primary sector extracts raw materials (farming, mining, fishing). Secondary processes raw materials (manufacturing), tertiary provides services, quaternary covers knowledge services.

questions.q: A Lagos exporter ships cocoa beans to a buyer in Hamburg under CIF terms. Which of the following is the exporter primarily responsible for paying?
options: Import duties in Germany
All costs until delivery to the buyer's factory
Freight and insurance to the named port in Hamburg
Unloading charges at the buyer's warehouse
questions.explanation: CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight) requires the exporter to pay costs of carriage and insurance to the destination port. The buyer pays import duties and unloading beyond the port unless otherwise agreed. Responsibility for delivery to the buyer's factory would be under a different Incoterm such as DDP.

questions.q: The Central Bank of Nigeria raises the official discount rate. Which immediate effect is most likely on foreign trade?
options: Customs duties are automatically reduced
Imports are likely to fall as higher interest rates strengthen the naira and raise local borrowing costs
Exports will increase because foreign buyers pay higher prices
Trade deficit will vanish immediately
questions.explanation: A higher discount rate tends to attract capital inflows, strengthening the naira and making imports cheaper but borrowing costlier for importers, which usually reduces import demand. It does not directly increase export prices, eliminate the trade deficit instantaneously, nor change customs duties (which are fiscal measures).

questions.q: A Nigerian company wants to reduce currency risk when selling to a European buyer who will pay in euros in three months. Which method best hedges the receivable?
options: Open a current account and wait for spot conversion in three months
Invoice in naira and ask the buyer to pay later
Buy a three-month call option on euros (right to buy euros)
Sell a three-month forward contract to lock in the naira/euro exchange rate
questions.explanation: Selling a forward contract locks the exchange rate for the future euro receivable, eliminating currency risk. Keeping a current account or invoicing in naira does not hedge exchange-rate movement; buying a call option gives the right to buy euros and would not hedge a euro receivable (the exporter needs to sell euros).

questions.q: If SANCO PLC issues bonus shares to existing shareholders, which of the following statements is true?
options: Shareholders must pay cash to receive the bonus shares
The total number of shares increases while the company's total equity remains the same
Each shareholder's percentage ownership decreases
Market price per share should ideally fall proportionally
questions.explanation: Bonus shares are capitalised from reserves: they increase the number of shares but do not change total equity, so existing ownership percentages remain the same. The market price per share normally falls proportionally, not necessarily stays unchanged; shareholders do not pay cash for bonus shares. Option claiming ownership decreases is incorrect.

questions.q: An investor bought 200 shares of a quoted oil company at ₦120 each. The company declared a dividend of ₦6 per share and the current market price is ₦150. What is the investor's dividend yield based on cost price?
questions.explanation: Dividend yield based on cost = (dividend per share ÷ cost per share) × 100 = (₦6 ÷ ₦120) × 100 = 5%. Using current market price would give (6 ÷ 150) × 100 = 4%, which is a common mistaken computation.

questions.q: Which function of the Nigerian Stock Exchange most directly helps companies raise long-term capital?
options: Setting retail prices for consumer goods
Providing a market for issuing and trading new shares (primary market listings)
Acting as an insurer for listed companies
Collecting customs duties for imported securities
questions.explanation: The stock exchange facilitates capital raising by allowing companies to list and issue shares to the public. It does not insure companies, set consumer prices, nor collect customs duties; those are unrelated functions.

questions.q: Mrs. Eze runs a retail shop in Enugu and buys goods from a wholesaler with payment terms of '2/10, net 30'. What is the financial benefit if she pays within 10 days on a ₦50,000 invoice?
options: She can take a 2% discount and pay ₦49,000
She pays ₦48,000 after a 4% discount
She will be charged ₦1,000 penalty for early payment
She must pay the full ₦50,000 regardless of when she pays
questions.explanation: Terms '2/10, net 30' mean a 2% discount if paid within 10 days. 2% of ₦50,000 = ₦1,000, so payable amount = ₦49,000. The other options misunderstand trade discounts or invent penalties or wrong percentages.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary function of the Central Bank of Nigeria?
options: Providing retail banking services to all citizens
Determining provincial tax rates
Running private pension funds
Regulating the nation's money supply and issuing currency
questions.explanation: Central banks control monetary policy, regulate money supply and issue currency. They do not provide retail banking services to the general public, set tax rates (a fiscal function), nor operate private pension funds.

questions.q: A customer places ₦500,000 in a fixed deposit account at 9% per annum simple interest for 18 months. What total interest will the bank pay?
questions.explanation: Simple interest = principal × rate × time (years). Time = 18 months = 1.5 years. So interest = ₦500,000 × 0.09 × 1.5 = ₦67,500. The other options are results of incorrect time or rate calculations (₦45,000 would be 1 year at 9%, ₦90,000 is 2 years at 9%).

questions.q: Which form of business ownership gives an entrepreneur full control, unlimited liability, and does not require registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission for small local operation in Lagos?
options: Public limited company
Private limited liability company
Sole proprietorship
Partnership
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned and controlled by one person who has unlimited liability and can operate without incorporation for small local businesses. A private limited company and public limited company require registration and limited liability; a partnership involves two or more owners sharing control and liability.

questions.q: A cooperative society of fishers in Rivers State pools resources and pays members dividends according to patronage. What main advantage does this type of business unit provide its members?
options: Ability to trade shares on the stock exchange
Centralised decision-making by an outside board
Lower costs through bulk purchasing and shared services
Unlimited liability protection for each member
questions.explanation: Cooperatives lower costs by bulk buying inputs and sharing services, and they distribute surplus to members by patronage. Members usually have limited liability depending on rules but not unlimited protection; cooperatives do not trade shares publicly like companies, nor are decisions typically centralised by outsiders.

questions.q: Which document sets out the internal rules, ownership structure and profit-sharing arrangement between partners in a Lagos-based trading partnership?
options: Articles of association
Partnership deed
Memorandum of association
Certificate of incorporation
questions.explanation: A partnership deed records partners' rights, duties, ownership shares and profit-sharing. Memorandum and Articles of Association and Certificate of Incorporation apply to companies, not ordinary partnerships.

questions.q: If a customer in Abeokuta buys a fridge that stops working within the seven-day statutory cooling-off period and the seller refuses a refund, which agency can the customer report to for redress?
options: Central Bank of Nigeria
Nigerian Immigration Service
Consumer Protection Council (now Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission)
Securities and Exchange Commission
questions.explanation: The Consumer Protection Council (now FCCPC) handles complaints about goods and services; SEC regulates capital markets, CBN handles banks, and Immigration deals with border matters, so those are inappropriate for consumer goods complaints.

questions.q: A retailer in Ibadan sells expired canned tomatoes without labelling. Under Nigerian consumer law this practice is primarily a breach of which consumer right?
options: Right to choose
Right to safety
Right to fair profit
Right to own property
questions.explanation: Selling expired food endangers consumers and breaches the right to safety. Right to choose concerns options of products, not safety; right to own property and right to fair profit are not relevant consumer protection rights in this context.

questions.q: Mr. Musa paid ₦45,000 for a radio but the battery compartment was missing. He returned it and demanded replacement. The shopkeeper offers repair in two weeks. What remedy is most appropriate immediately?
options: Rejection and refund due to non-conformity
Accept repair and demand partial refund
Exchange for unrelated item of same price
Accept repair and wait two weeks
questions.explanation: A product missing a key component is non-conforming; the buyer may reject and demand a refund or replacement. Waiting for repair may be acceptable but not most appropriate immediately; exchange for an unrelated item or partial refund without agreement are not standard remedies.

questions.q: Which mode of transport is generally most cost-effective for moving heavy bulk commodities like cement from Lagos to Kano overland?
options: Air transport
Rail transport
Courier van
Sea transport
questions.explanation: Rail is most cost-effective for heavy bulk overland distances due to low per-ton costs. Air is very costly, sea cannot deliver inland without further land transport, and courier vans are for small parcels, not bulk cargo.

questions.q: A Lagos exporter sends documents by courier to a buyer in Accra. He needs proof of dispatch and delivery with timestamps. Which communication service best meets this need?
options: Registered courier service with tracking and proof of delivery
Broadcast radio announcement
Standard express email
Ordinary postal letter
questions.explanation: A registered courier with tracking provides timestamps and proof of delivery. Express email gives electronic transmission but not physical delivery proof; ordinary post lacks reliable tracking, and radio announcements are irrelevant.

questions.q: A cosmetics firm in Kaduna uses a celebrity in a TV advert claiming their cream 'removes all wrinkles overnight'. Which advertising issue is most likely raised?
options: Misleading claim about product performance
Breach of transport regulations
Violation of copyright law
Illegal use of foreign exchange
questions.explanation: An absolute claim of overnight removal of wrinkles is likely misleading and may breach advertising standards. It is not primarily a copyright, foreign exchange, or transport regulation issue.

questions.q: A startup in Enugu targets only university students with budget skincare packs and advertises mainly on campus noticeboards. Which marketing strategy are they using?
options: Market segmentation and niche targeting
Undifferentiated pricing strategy
Mass marketing to heterogeneous market
Vertical integration
questions.explanation: Focusing on university students with specific products is market segmentation and niche targeting. Mass marketing would target everyone; undifferentiated pricing ignores segments; vertical integration refers to control of supply chain, not targeting customers.

questions.q: Mrs. Okonkwo runs an online boutique in Enugu. She sells a dress for ₦18,000 and allows customers to pay by card through an e-payment gateway that charges 1.5% per transaction plus a fixed charge of ₦50. What amount does Mrs. Okonkwo receive into her account after the gateway fee is deducted?
questions.explanation: Compute 1.5% of ₦18,000 = ₦270, then subtract the percentage fee and the fixed ₦50: ₦18,000 − ₦270 − ₦50 = ₦17,680. The first wrong option omitted the fixed charge, the third used an incorrect rate (2%).

questions.q: A Lagos bookstore sells e-books and uses a subscription model with monthly recurring billing. Which practice most reduces customer churn for this digital retailer?
options: Offering personalised recommendations and periodic exclusive content to subscribers
Removing payment options to force annual billing only
Charging higher prices to long-term subscribers
Limiting customer support to email only
questions.explanation: Personalisation and exclusive content increase perceived value and engagement, reducing churn. The wrong options either worsen customer experience (higher prices, fewer payment options, poor support) and would likely increase churn.

questions.q: An online vendor in Port Harcourt collects customers' email addresses and behavioural data without clear consent. Under good e-commerce practice and consumer protection, this is primarily a breach of what?
options: Data protection and privacy principles requiring informed consent
Tax law for unreported digital sales
Contract law because emails are not legal documents
Competition law regulating market dominance
questions.explanation: Collecting personal data without informed consent violates data protection and privacy principles. It's not directly a competition, contract, or tax issue, though those areas may become relevant in other contexts.

questions.q: Mr. Ade insured his shop stock for ₦600,000 with an average clause and the insurer pays claims on average basis. At time of fire the actual stock value was ₦1,200,000 and the loss was ₦300,000. How much will the insurer pay?
options: Insurer pays proportion = insured ÷ actual value = ₦600,000/₦1,200,000 = 1/2. So payment = 1/2 × ₦300,000 = ₦150,000
₦600,000 (insured amount)
₦300,000 (full loss)
₦75,000 (1/4 of the loss)
questions.explanation: With average clause, payment is insured/actual value = 600,000/1,200,000 = 0.5 of the loss. So 0.5 × 300,000 = ₦150,000. Paying the full loss or insured amount ignores pro rata adjustment; ₦75,000 is wrong fraction.

questions.q: A motor insurance policy in Abuja covers 'third-party, fire and theft' but not damage to the insured's own car in an accident. Which of the following is true?
options: The insurer will only pay for injuries to the policyholder
The insurer will pay for injury to other people and for the insured car if it is stolen or damaged by fire, but not for collision damage to the insured car
The insurer will pay for all damage to the insured car including collision
The insurer will refuse all claims arising from the policyholder's negligence
questions.explanation: 'Third-party, fire and theft' policies cover liability to others and losses from fire or theft to the insured car, but not collision damage to the insured's vehicle. The wrong options either overstate cover, confuse negligence exclusions, or misidentify beneficiaries.

questions.q: A supplier in Kano sends goods to a buyer in Accra. Which document, when endorsed and handed to the buyer's bank, transfers title to the goods and allows the buyer to claim the cargo at destination?
options: Certificate of origin
Bill of lading endorsed to order
Pro forma invoice
Commercial invoice only (unsigned)
questions.explanation: A bill of lading, when endorsed to order, is a document of title allowing transfer and release of goods; a commercial invoice is for payment/valuation, a pro forma is an offer, and a certificate of origin proves origin but does not transfer title.

questions.q: Which document most commonly serves as proof that goods were despatched from a seller's warehouse and lists quantities and weights for a buyer in Jos?
options: Delivery note or dispatch note showing items and weights
Certificate of incorporation of the seller
Letter of credit issued by buyer's bank
Insurance policy (which proves shipment)
questions.explanation: A delivery or dispatch note records items sent from the seller's warehouse including quantities and weights. Insurance policies, letters of credit, and company incorporation certificates do not provide dispatch details.

questions.q: A factory in Ibadan employs 40 workers who produce 8,000 units weekly. If management hires 10 more workers and keeps productivity per worker constant, what is the new weekly output?
options: Productivity per worker = 8,000 ÷ 40 = 200 units. With 50 workers → 50 × 200 = 10,000 units
12,000 units (assuming productivity doubles)
8,800 units (10% increase)
9,000 units (assuming 10 extra workers add 1,000 units)
questions.explanation: Per-worker output = 8,000/40 = 200 units. Adding 10 workers at same productivity gives 50 × 200 = 10,000 units. The other options assume incorrect percentage changes or unrealistic productivity shifts.

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'division of labour' in a Lagos garment workshop?
options: Rotating workers daily so each learns every task
Paying workers only when finished product sells
Breaking the production process into small specialised tasks so each worker repeats one task
Outsourcing all production to foreign firms
questions.explanation: Division of labour assigns specialised, repetitive tasks to workers to raise efficiency. Rotating workers is the opposite, outsourcing is contracting out, and pay terms relate to compensation not division of labour.

questions.q: An entreprenuer in Benin City wants to raise labour productivity. Which action is most likely to increase productivity per worker without increasing hours?
options: Lowering wages to discourage absenteeism
Reducing product quality to speed up production
Replacing workers with untrained casual labour
Providing training and better tools to reduce time per unit produced
questions.explanation: Training and better tools increase skills and efficiency, raising output per worker. Lowering wages can harm morale, reducing quality is counterproductive long-term, and replacing with untrained labour typically lowers productivity.

questions.q: A sole proprietorship is often chosen by small traders in Lagos because it offers which main advantage?
options: It allows easy transfer of ownership through sale of shares
It requires complex legal formalities to start
Owner's decisions are taken quickly and profits belong entirely to the owner
It limits the owner's personal liability for business debts
questions.explanation: Sole proprietorships give the owner full control and entitlement to all profits, allowing quick decisions. It does not limit personal liability (owner has unlimited liability), does not involve shares (so ownership transfer via shares is not applicable), and is usually easy to start rather than legally complex.

questions.q: A limited liability company in Nigeria issues 100,000 ordinary shares at ₦50 each. If the company receives ₦4,000,000 in paid-up capital, what percentage of shares has been paid for?
Mrs. Adebayo bought a gas cooker in Ibadan that malfunctioned within the 30-day warranty. Under consumer protection principles, her best immediate action is to:
options: Return the cooker to the seller with receipt and request repair or replacement
Burn the receipt and demand full refund without showing proof of purchase
Ignore the seller and ask the manufacturer to pay compensation directly
Resell the cooker cheaply and claim a refund from the seller
questions.explanation: Consumer protection gives the buyer the right to repair, replacement or refund when a product fails within warranty; returning the item with proof of purchase is the correct immediate step. Burning the receipt removes evidence; manufacturers may direct you to the seller; reselling the faulty item prevents legitimate remedy.

questions.q: For transporting 40 tonnes of cement from Lagos to Kano, which mode is generally most cost-effective and why?
options: Air transport, because it is fastest and therefore cheapest for heavy bulk
Pipeline transport, because it is suitable for solid goods like cement
Water transport, because inland water routes exist directly between Lagos and Kano
Road transport, because it offers door-to-door delivery for short-to-medium inland distances at reasonable cost
questions.explanation: For 40 tonnes moved within Nigeria, road transport is usually most cost-effective and practical due to door-to-door capability. Air is fastest but very costly for heavy bulk. There is no direct inland water route between Lagos and Kano for such freight, and pipelines are for liquids/gases, not solid goods like cement.

questions.q: A Kaduna firm runs an advert claiming its soap 'makes skin flawless after one wash' without clinical proof. This claim is likely to be considered which type of advertising practice?
options: Informative advertising because it provides factual consumer information
Puffery because it uses vague, harmless exaggeration that cannot be tested
Comparative advertising because it directly compares the soap with competitors
Misleading advertising because it makes unverified absolute claims about product performance
questions.explanation: An absolute unverified claim about performance is misleading advertising; it can deceive consumers. Comparative adverts explicitly compare brands (not present), puffery is vague and non-testable (this claim is testable and specific), and informative adverts provide factual, verifiable details rather than strong performance claims.
